finding_dispositions.evidence: Fresh r8 verifier rebuild/replay, full gate, and targeted tests passed for no-follow initialization, fanout, and post-initialization objects/staging/locks/resources replacement. Descriptor-bound operations reject replaced attested ancestors before external mutation.

The freshly rerun clock regression passed: expiry observation persists repository-owned high-water state, and subsequent clock rollback cannot revive an expired lease. Authoritative time decisions remain transactionally bound to persisted high-water state.

Fresh canonical resource-order and opposing-process tests passed. Cross-token acquisition rejects decreasing resource sequences before mutation, and opposing two-process requests terminate without deadlock or partial acquisition.

The fresh exact claim/reconciliation regression passed. Direct CommitBatch validation binds the complete ordered lease-resource set, fence tokens, task lease, and same-transaction event payload, including missing, extra, empty, stale, and wrong-lease rejection.
Fresh full evidence replay passed the doctor and backup read-only cases. Read-only URI, query_only, and deny-by-default authorizer continue to reject direct and WITH-prefixed writes.

Fresh replay/recovery corruption regressions passed. Event indexes, transaction revisions, transaction heads, and task/head state remain validated against authoritative replay and fail closed on corruption.

Fresh r8 replacement and fault regressions passed at object.after_staging_directory_fsync and object.after_publication: wrong staging/final names are cleared, no invalid available metadata remains, and post-commit mismatch is quarantined.

Fresh stateful dedup regressions at object.after_object_directory_fsync and object.before_metadata_commit passed: the current transaction rolls back, preexisting available metadata is durably quarantined, and wrong final/staging names are cleared. Normal dedup, fresh, post-commit, and 13-step-by-3-kind fault paths also passed.

Fresh gate-bound two-writer regressions passed at both stale-cleanup windows: writer B cannot pass writer A's same-digest publication lock, then succeeds after A releases; final bytes are readable, metadata is available, and staging is empty. Publication remains exclusive across threads/processes, while cleanup records the mismatched device/inode and only unlinks a still-matching observed name.

r8 gives publication a distinct filename namespace and fixed lock rank after all action resources and before object maintenance. Independent public-API probes held outer installation plus valid resource sets on both lexical sides, persisted verified objects, and observed byte-for-byte identical outer token stacks before and after; put_verified did not release or perturb caller tokens. A contended publication probe failed atomically with the outer token stack intact and succeeded after release, and same textual business/publication identities map to distinct lock files. Fresh thread/process tests confirm exact-digest exclusion without resource ordering dependence, reentrancy, or partial acquisition.
